name: Political instability
summary: No G20 government collapse or coup; US midterms on 3 Nov
state: No G20 government has fallen and no coup was reported as of 2 Nov. France saw a third weekend of mass protests on 31 Oct with clashes in several cities, and protests in Germany turned violent on 1 Nov (Bloomberg). The US holds midterm elections on 3 Nov.
for_you: Political risk is building rather than acute. A French government collapse would likely push its borrowing costs higher.
rubric_hit: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in the past month

sources.title: The Japan Times — Clashes break out as hundreds of thousands protest in France
Bloomberg — German protests turn violent as activists clash with police

why: Coups, contested elections and constitutional crises in large economies unsettle markets, alliances and policy.
drivers: Elections, government collapses, coups, emergency rule, mass protest movements.

rubric.alert: Coup or constitutional crisis in a G20 country, or deadly unrest threatening a G20 government.
rubric.watch: Government collapse or contested election in a G20 country, or a coup anywhere.
rubric.normal: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in the past month.
